svg.text: How the fly brain drives the car
One control step, covering 0.1 s of simulated time. A frozen 166,700-neuron fly connectome sits in the middle; the only learned part is the readout at the end.
Every 0.1 s the car moves, the rays change, and the brain takes another step.

Why route A is slow: it steers reasonably (R² 0.62), but on ~54% of frames it asks for less than the
0.05 minimum acceleration, so the car crawls. Route B learns acceleration from reward instead.
Source: docs/fly-brain-driver-how-it-works.md. Figures were read off the running system on 2026-09-21.
